newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila eyes supplemental budget to pay oil firms.
newsitem.headline: Manila eyes supplemental budget to pay oil firms.

text.p: The Philippines is considering a 2.4 billion peso supplemental budget to reimburse the claims of the country's oil refiners, finance secretary Roberto de Ocampo said on Wednesday.

De Ocampo said the government has agreed in principle to push for the early payment of claims against the state-managed Oil Price Stabilisation Fund (OPSF) through the passage of a supplemental budget.
The Congress has yet to approve the 1997 general budget due to bickering over fund allocations.
De Ocampo said if the supplemental budget will not be passed as part of the 1997 budget, the government will include the claims in the 1998 budget proposal.
OPSF was a buffer fund created to reduce the impact of international oil price fluctuations on the local market.

The country's three main oil companies -- Petron Corp, Caltex Philippines Inc and Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp -- contributed to it when the international prices were low and drew against it when the prices went up.
With international prices outstripping the controlled local prices in recent months, the OPSF has slipped into deficit.
